(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 09.03.2022 passed by the III Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge & MACT, Kalaburagi in MVC No.645/2019

. 
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 18.10.2018 at about 7.30 pm.,
when the deceased Malappa was proceeding on his bike to his village, on the Jewargi-Sindagi main road, near KGN Dhabha, at that time, a lorry bearing registration No. GJ- 12/BV-9553 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7460-DB HC-KAR 3.
The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.22,55,664/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the claimants contended that the deceased was a meritorious student and had completed his Bachelor of physical Education in the year 2013.
It was further submitted that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month by giving tuition.
The accident occurred in the year 2018, at that time deceased was aged about 33 years.
However, the assessment of the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.
Considering the age and the avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, the learned counsel sought for enhancement of compensation.
7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the deceased had completed his Bachelor of Physical Education in the year 2013.

Even after the lapse of five years, he had not obtained any employment, and there is no pleading to indicate that he was applying for a job as a Physical NC: 2025:KHC-K:7460-DB HC-KAR Education teacher.
Although the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, they have failed to substantiate their claim with supporting documents.
Therefore, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased.
Considering the age and the avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, learned counsel sought for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that the deceased Malappa died in the road traffic accident occurred on 18.10.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. The case of the claimants is that the deceased had completed his Bachelor of Physical Education in the year 2013.
The accident occurred in the year 2018, at that NC: 2025:KHC-K:7460-DB HC-KAR time, the deceased was aged about 33 years.
However, neither in their evidence nor in their pleadings, the claimants have indicated that the deceased was searching for a job or applying for any job, nor have they produced any offer letter.
The only assertion made is that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month by giving tuition to students but no supporting documents or bank statements have been produced.

11. Considering all these aspects, and in the absence of documentary evidence, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.11,750/- per month and added 40%
towards 'future prospects'.
Considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
The appellant has not made out any case seeking for enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7460-DB HC-KAR 12.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed confirming the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

Sd/-
